The fog had been rolling in off the North Sea for three days, thick enough to swallow the horizon whole. Elias Thorne, the lighthouse keeper of Gull’s Point, had grown accustomed to the isolation, but the silence of the storm was different. It was a heavy, suffocating quiet that pressed against the glass of the lantern room.

Elias was polishing the Fresnel lens, a ritual he had performed for twenty years, when the light flickered. Not a mechanical stutter, but a rhythmic pulse. *Blink. Blink. Blink.*

He frowned, wiping a smudge from the glass. The main beam, which should have been a steady, sweeping arc of white, was stuttering in a pattern that didn’t match the rotation of the lamp. He checked the clockwork mechanism. It was smooth. He checked the oil levels. They were full.

He stepped back, his breath fogging in the cold air. The light pulsed again. *Blink. Blink. Blink.*

Elias frowned. It wasn’t Morse code. It was too slow, too deliberate. He grabbed his notebook and a pencil, his hands trembling slightly. He began to count the intervals. One second on, two seconds off. One
